questions.question: In general, riders should:

options.text: Pick one lane position and always use it.
Change lane positions frequently to prevent monotony.
Choose a lane position that gives them the most space around their bike.
Never use the center lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Choose a lane position that gives them the most space around their bike.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change constantly. The safest lane position also changes. Choose the position that gives you the most space around your bike and lets other drivers see you best.

questions.question: More than half of all motorcycle crashes:

options.text: Happen at night.
Are caused by bald tires.
Occur at speeds above 55 mph.
Involve inexperienced riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Involve inexperienced riders.
questions.explanation: More than half of all motorcycle crashes involve riders who have owned their motorcycle for less than six months. Most crashes happen during the day when riders are going slowly.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger or cargo:

options.text: It may take less time to accelerate, but more time to stop.
It may take more time to accelerate and stop.
It may take more time to accelerate, but less time to stop.
It may take less time to accelerate and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may take more time to accelerate and stop.
questions.explanation: Extra weight from cargo or a passenger makes it take longer for a motorcycle to accelerate and stop compared to riding alone.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
Provide a good view of the shoulder.
Provide a poor view of road hazards.
Invite others to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and helps them see you. Do not ride in another driver's blind spot for long periods of time.

questions.question: When riding downhill on a motorcycle with a sidecar:

options.text: Stopping will be easier than when riding without a sidecar.
Stopping will take longer than when riding without a sidecar.
You cannot stop.
Stopping is about as easy as it is when riding without the sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping will take longer than when riding without a sidecar.
questions.explanation: A sidecar adds weight to your motorcycle, which means you need more braking force to stop. Stopping takes longer when going downhill than on flat ground.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle properly, you should:

options.text: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up.
Sit far enough back on the seat that you can keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Drag your feet on the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up.
questions.explanation: Sit so your arms control the motorcycle instead of holding you up. Your arms should bend slightly when holding the handgrips. Keep your knees against the gas tank and your feet on the footrests to help with balance.

questions.question: When passing a row of parked cars on your right with no oncoming traffic on your left, you should:

options.text: Stay toward the right side of your lane.
Stay toward the left side of your lane.
Look to your left frequently.
Use your rearview mirrors more frequently than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay toward the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: When passing parked cars, stay on the side of your lane away from the cars. This protects you from car doors opening or people stepping out from between cars. If traffic is coming toward you, stay in the center of your lane.

questions.question: Where is the engine cut-off switch usually located?

options.text: Near the left handgrip
Near the right handgrip
Near the left footrest
Near the right footrest

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right handgrip
questions.explanation: The engine cut-off switch is usually next to the right handgrip. Learn where all your motorcycle's controls are before you start riding.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a good way to increase your visibility as a rider?

options.text: Wearing proper clothing
Using your headlight at all times
Using your turn signals
Waving at other drivers

questions.correctAnswerText: Waving at other drivers
questions.explanation: To be more visible, wear bright or reflective clothing, use your headlight at all times, and use your signals and brake light correctly.

questions.question: Reflective clothing should:

options.text: Be worn only at night.
Be worn only during the day.
Not be worn.
Be worn day and night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be worn day and night.
questions.explanation: Bright and reflective clothing helps you be seen in all conditions. Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day, so wearing bright clothing during the day is important too.

questions.question: What does eye contact with another driver mean?

options.text: The driver sees you.
The driver may not yield to you.
The driver will definitely yield to you.
The driver may become angry.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver may not yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume a driver will yield just because they make eye contact with you. Drivers often look at motorcyclists but still do not see them.

questions.question: Why should motorcycle riders not rely only on mirrors?

options.text: Motorcycle mirrors are smaller and show less area.
Motorcycles have blind spots like all vehicles.
Mirrors are never accurate.
Mirrors take your eyes off the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots like all vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots. You cannot see everything behind you using mirrors alone. Check over your shoulder frequently as part of your normal riding routine.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The rider will turn left.
The rider will stop.
The rider will turn right.
The rider will slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: The rider will turn left.
questions.explanation: Riders use hand signals instead of turn signals. A left arm extended straight to the left means the rider will turn left or change lanes to the left.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, what should you do?

options.text: Keep your normal following distance.
Brake later than usual.
Ride slower than usual.
Ride faster than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride slower than usual.
questions.explanation: The extra weight of a passenger makes your motorcycle sit lower. Ride slower than usual, especially around curves and bumps. Your motorcycle will need more time to speed up, slow down, and stop. Keep more space between you and other vehicles.

questions.question: Which action will NOT reduce your chance of an accident?

options.text: Staying alert.
Spotting hazards and deciding what to address first.
Riding without a headlight.
Keeping space around your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding without a headlight.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, stay alert and ready to react. Spot hazards and prioritize them. Always use your headlight to be more visible. Keep space cushion around your motorcycle at all times.

questions.question: Where is the horn button usually located?

options.text: Near the left handgrip.
Near the right handgrip.
Near the left footrest.
Near the right footrest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the left handgrip.
questions.explanation: Learn where all your motorcycle controls are before you start riding. The horn button is usually located next to the left handgrip.

questions.question: If a dog chases you on your motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Kick at it.
Stop and wait for it to lose interest.
Swerve around it.
Slow down, get close, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, get close, then speed up.
questions.explanation: If a dog chases you, downshift and approach it slowly. Once close, accelerate and leave it behind. Do not try to kick the dog.

questions.question: What is a danger of braking too hard?

options.text: Your wheels may lose grip on the road.
You may stop sooner than expected.
Your tire may burst.
You may take too long to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your wheels may lose grip on the road.
questions.explanation: Braking too hard can cause you to lose traction on one or both wheels and crash.

questions.question: How should you brake during normal stopping?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.
Switch between front and rear brakes to make them last longer.
Use both the front and rear brakes together.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes together.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes together every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When turning on a motorcycle, where should you look?

options.text: Keep your eyes on the road just ahead of your front tire.
Look ahead through the turn to where you want to go.
Turn your entire body to see through the turn.
Speed up before entering the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead through the turn to where you want to go.
questions.explanation: Look ahead through the turn to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders, and keep your eyes level with the horizon.
